content.rendered:
11:24 p.m. The Senate adjourned.

11:14 p.m. Democratic Leader Schumer spoke on the 119th Congress thus far.

11:01 p.m. Majority Leader Thune wrapped up for the evening.

Passed the following bills: S.3315, Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act of 2026 with Cassidy substitute; S.2273– Wyoming Education Trust Modernization Act; H.R.5235 – Skills-Based Federal Contracting Act; S.5249 – MORE American Fuel Act; ; S.2437 – Snow Water Supply Forecasting Program Reauthorization Act of 2026; S.1514 – Quinault Indian Nation Land Transfer Act; H.R.2400 – Pit River Land Transfer Act of 2025; S.1055 – Indian Health Service Emergency Claims Parity Act; S.1564 – Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act; H.R.227 – Clergy Act; H.R.1703 – Choices For Increased Mobility; H.R.4307 – Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act; H.R.8352 – Criminal History Access Act of 2026  

Adopted the following resolutions:S.Res.866 – Substance Use and Misuse Prevention Month; S.Res.936 – Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day; S.Res.937 – PCOS Awareness Month; S.Res.938 – October 7; S.Res.939 – Iowa-Kosovo; S.Res.940 – Sickle Cell Disease Awareness Month; S.Res.941 – Bat Week; S.Res.942 – National Forensic Science Week; S.Res.943 – National Move Over Law Day; S.Res.944 – School Bus Safety Month; S.Res.945 – Bison Day; S.Res.946 – National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day; S.Res.947 – Childhood Cancer Awareness Month; S.Res.948– Texas A&M 150th Anniversary.

Completed the Rule 14 process to place the following bills on the Legislative Calendar:

  1. S.5602, to prohibit the use of Federal funds for the planning and construction of any structure or monument at Memorial Circle at Columbia Island/ Lady Bird Johnson Park in the District of Columbia. (Merkley)
  2. S.5603, to prohibit the demolition of Presidential memorials (Merkley)

Executive Business

Confirmed the following nominations:AIR FORCE: Executive Cal. #913 – Brig. Gen. Stephen P. Snelson to be Major General;

11:00 p.m. The Senate confirmed the Sonderling nomination on a party line vote of 47-41.
Republicans not voting: Blackburn, Cornyn, Ernst, McConnell, Moran & Tillis.
Democrats not voting: Blumenthal, Durbin, Gillibrand, Smith, Warner & Whitehouse.

9:29 p.m. The Senate began voting on confirmation of the nomination of Keith Sonderling to be Secretary of Labor.

9:19 p.m. Senator Cortez-Masto spoke about the Inspector General for Federal Housing Finance Agency. She asked for unanimous consent to proceed to and pass S.5681. Senator Moreno objected.

9:09 p.m. Senator Hoeven asked consent to take up and pass H.R. 1829, regarding public land management. Senator Heinrich objected.

9:00 p.m. Senator Coons spoke about AI regulation. He then moved to discuss and by unanimous consent to take up and pass HR 9496, the “Stop Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act”.

8:43 p.m. Senator Cornyn spoke about H.R. 7022-provide for transmission of energy alerts by satellite. The bill passed by unanimous consent.

8:33 p.m. Senator Shaheen spoke about ambassador nominations. She sought unanimous consent to proceed to and confirm 10 ambassadors. The following nominations were confirmed en bloc:

  • PN1255-12-Peter Lord to Ambassador to Benin
  • PN1255-9-Keith Heffern to Ambassador to Gaban
  • PN1022-36-Daniel Travis to be Ambassador to Sierra Leone
  • PN1022-39-Henry Wooster to be Ambassador to Kenya
  • PN1201-4-Joshua Harris to be Ambassador to Malaysia
  • PN1255-15-Nuton Patel to be Ambassador to Cabo Verde
  • PN1255-7-Steven Gillen to be Ambassador to the Kyrgyz Republic
  • PN1255-8-Charles Goodman III to be Ambassador to Togo
  • PN1255-13-John McIntyre to be Ambassador to Malawi
  • PN1255-6-Natasha Franceschi to be Ambassador to Nicaragua

8:31 p.m. Senator Cassidy spoke about the Healthcare Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act-S. 3315.

8:15 p.m. Senator Lankford spoke about the Hyde amendment.

7:40 p.m. Senator Bennet spoke on the American dream, President Trump, and wealth inequality.

7:35 p.m. Senator Lee achieved consent to take up and pass H.R. 6380, to redesignate the Cherry Kohua National Monument; he then achieved consent to pass H.R 837 (To require the Secretary of Agriculture to convey the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site to Gila County, Arizona) and H.R. 7831 (License to Drill Act) en bloc. He then discussed the permitting reform deal announced earlier today.

7:22 p.m. Senators Lankford and Merkley debated voter ID.

7:02 p.m. Senator Merkley spoke on and asked unanimous consent to take up and pass a bill banning members of Congress and the President and Vice President from trading stocks. Senator Lankford objected.

6:22 p.m. Senators Murray, Kaine, Shaheen, and Baldwin spoke about pocket rescissions. Senator Merkley asked for unanimous consent that the Senate proceed to and pass S. 5670. Senator Johnson objected.

6:13 p.m. Senator Merkley spoke about the power of the purse.

6:02 p.m. Senator Hassan spoke about gas prices, healthcare, and high prices.

5:39 p.m. Senators Schmitt and Moody spoke about fraud. Senator Schmitt asked unanimous consent to proceed to and pass. H.R. 9576. Senator Whitehouse objected and asked that the bill be modified. Senator Schmitt objected.

5:24 p.m. Senator Wyden spoke on public lands and asked unanimous consent for the Senate to pass S.5658. Senator Paul objected.

5:07 p.m. Senator Blumenthal spoke on Ukraine as well as kids online safety. He then asked unanimous consent for the Senate to pass S.1748, Kids Online Safety Act. Senator Paul objected.

4:40 p.m. Senators Tillis, Curtis, and Armstrong spoke on Ukraine.

4:03 p.m. Senator Blackburn spoke on gender and sports. She then requested unanimous consent for the Senate to agree to S.Res.934. Senator Markey objected.

3:54 p.m. Senators Wyden and Crapo spoke on taxes. Senator Crapo then asked unanimous consent to pass H.R. 5349, as amended by the Crapo-Wyden amendment. It passed by unanimous consent.

3:50 p.m. Senator Cruz spoke on the Federal Bank Robbery Act. The Senate then passed S.3798, Safe Access to Cash Act of 2026, by voice vote.

3:32 p.m. Senator Blackburn and Senator Coons spoke on their bipartisan legislation on AI deepfakes. Senator Blackburn then requested unanimous consent to pass S.4591 with the Committee reported substitute amendment; Senator Cruz objected.

2:55 p.m. Senator Ernst spoke about fraud and asked unanimous consent for the Senate to pass S.4952, Protecting American Taxpayers Act. Senator Wyden objected.

2:47 p.m. Senator Rosen spoke about Canadian tariffs. She asked for unanimous consent that the Senate proceed to and pass S. Res. 898. Senator Crapo objected.

2:43 p.m. The following bills, as amended, were passed en bloc:

  • S. 2498-National Park System Long-Term Lease Investment Act
  • S. 2754-Crystal Reservoir Conveyance Act

2:22 p.m. Senator Murphy spoke on immigration enforcement. He asked for unanimous consent to proceed to and pass S. 5345. Senator Banks objected and spoke about ICE.

2:21 p.m. The Senate invoked cloture on the nomination of Keith Sonderling to be Secretary of Labor.

1:41 p.m. By a party-line vote of 53-47, the Senate began voting on cloture on the nomination of Keith Sonderling to be Secretary of Labor (30 hours of post-cloture debate).

1:40 p.m. The Senate did not invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 9340 by a tally of 57-43.
Democrats voting in favor: Hassan, Klobuchar, Ossoff, and Warnock.

12:51 p.m. The Senate began voting on cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act.

12:50 p.m. The Senate did not invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 7008 on a party line tally of 53-47.

11:58 a.m. The Senate is now voting on the Motion to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R.7008, Stop Insider Trading Act.

11:56 a.m. Senator Heinrich spoke on the cost of utility bills and data centers.

11:31 a.m. Senator Sullivan spoke on the Alaska Right to Produce Act 2.0. He then asked unanimous consent to pass S. 5438; Senator Heinrich objected. Senator Sullivan spoke more on Alaska.

11:18 a.m. Senator Budd spoke on Hurricane Helene. He then asked unanimous consent to pass H.R.4238, Disaster Loan Accountability and Reform Act or the DLARA; Senator Markey objected.

11:14 a.m. Senator Ricketts spoke on insider trading.

11:08 a.m. Senator Hagerty spoke on data centers and innovation.

10:59 a.m. Senator Husted spoke on data centers.

10:49 a.m. Senator Padilla spoke on the pending stock trading bill and voter ID.

10:36 a.m. Democratic Leader Schumer spoke on the 119th Congress, the AI meeting at the White House on Tuesday; the pending stock trading bill, and paid tribute to departing staffer Cietta Kiandoli.

10:22 a.m. Majority Leader Thune moved to proceed to H.R. 9340, amending the Public Utility Act of 1978.
The following two bills had their first reading: S 5602, to prohibit the use of Federal funds for the planning and construction of any structure or monument at Memorial Circle at Columbia Island/ Lady Bird Johnson Park and S. 5603 prohibiting the demolition of Presidential memorials.
Leader Thune then spoke on the stock trading bill and the ratepayer protection act.

10:15 a.m. The Senate convened.

*****

The Senate will convene at 10:15 a.m. Following Leader Remarks, the Senate will be in a period of Morning Business with Senators permitted to speak therein for up to 10 minutes each.

At 11:30 a.m., the Senate is expected to proceed to the following roll call votes:

  1. Motion to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R.7008, Stop Insider Trading Act. If cloture is not invoked, then:
  2. Motion to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R.9340, Ratepayer Protection Act. If cloture is not invoked, then:
  3. Motion to invoke cloture on the nomination of Keith Sonderling to be Secretary of Labor.

Additional votes are possible during today’s session of the Senate.

8:15 p.m. The Senate stands adjourned until 10:15 a.m. on Wednesday. With Leader remarks reserved, the Senate will proceed to morning business. At 11:30 a.m. the Senate will proceed to up to three roll call votes.

  1. Motion to invoke cloture on the MTP to H.R.7008, Stop Insider Trading Act.
  2. (If cloture is not invoked) Motion to invoke cloture on the MTP to H.R.9340, Ratepayer Protection Act.
  3. (If cloture is not invoked) Motion to invoke cloture on Executive Calendar #912, Keith Sonderling, of Florida, to be Secretary of Labor.

Majority Leader Thune wrapped up.

  1. The following bills received their first reading:
    • S. 5602 – A bill to prohibit the use of federal funds for any structure of monument at memorial circle at Lady Bird Johnson Park in the District of Columbia.
  2. Passed by unanimous consent: S.528 – the GLRI Act of 2025,with the Peters substitute amendment.
  3. Passed by unanimous consent: S.1574 – Tribal Access to Electronic Evidence Act, with the Cortez-Masto substitute amendment.
  4. Passed by unanimous consent: H.R. 5284 – Claiming Age Clarity Act.
  5. Passed by unanimous consent: H.R. 1190 – Expanding Access to Capital for Rural Job Creators Act.
  6. Passed by voice vote: S.5600 – To Reauthorize the Traumatic Brain Injury Program.
  7. Agreed to en bloc by unanimous consent: S. Res. 922, S. Res. 923, S. Res. 924, S. Res. 925, S. Res. 926, S. Res. 927, S. Res. 928.
  8. Agreed to by unanimous consent: S. Res. 652 – A resolution honoring the life and service of United States Marine Corps veteran Nicholas Douglas Quets, expressing condolences to his family, and condemning cartel violence.
  9. Passed by unanimous consent: H.R. 1744 – United States Commission on International Religious Freedom Reauthorization Act of 2026
  10. Passed by unanimous consent: H.R. 10159 – To authorize the Secretary of the Army to convey to the State of North Carolina a certain parcel of real property located at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, on which the State shall construct a veterans’ State home, and for other purposes.

8:08 p.m. By a vote of 47-51, the Senate did not discharge S. Res. 852 – A resolution requesting information on Israel’s human rights practices.

  • Senator Fetterman (D) voted no and Senator Paul (R) voted aye.
  • Senators Cassidy and Sullivan did not vote.

6:30 p.m. The Senate began voting on the previously scheduled roll call vote on the motion to discharge S. Res. 852 from the Foreign Relations Committee.

6:20 p.m. Senator Welch spoke on S.Res.852 and Gaza.

6:01 p.m. Senator Van Hollen called up S.Res.852 and spoke on Israeli human rights practices.

5:55 p.m. Senator Sanders spoke on S.Res.852 and American sentiment on Isreal.

5:39 p.m. Senator Paul spoke on Israeli human rights practices. He then asked for unanimous consent to pass his related bill, which is at the secretary’s desk; Senator Van Hollen objected.

5:29 p.m. Senator Kaine spoke on Israeli human rights practices.

5:19 p.m. Senator Daines spoke on S.Res.852.

5:14 p.m. Senator Young spoke on insider trader for members of congress.

5:03 p.m. Senator Warner spoke on artificial intelligence and data centers.

4:47 p.m. Senator Hassan spoke on the taxpayer-funded advertisements for President Trump and asked unanimous consent to take up and pass S. Res. 921 on this topic; Senator Lummis objected.

4:37 p.m. Senator Curtis achieved unanimous consent that the Senate will vote on a Van Hollen motion to discharge S. Res. 852 from the Foreign Relations Committee at 7:00 p.m.

4:25 p.m. Senators Merkley, Padilla and Curtis spoke on wildfires and the Wildfire Prevention Act and achieved unanimous consent for the Senate to pass S. 5045, the Wildfire Prevention Act.

4:17 p.m. Senator Curtis spoke on water issues in the west.

4:13 p.m.. Senator Rosen spoke on the upcoming 9th anniversary of the mass shooting in Las Vegas on October 1, 2017.

3:57 p.m. Senator Coons spoke on the Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act.

3:48 p.m. Senator Murkowski spoke on the South Central Foundation Land Transfer Act and achieved unanimous consent for the Senate to pass the following bills en bloc:

  • H.R.3620 – Southcentral Foundation Land Transfer Act of 2025.
  • S.3383 – Unlocking Native Lands and Opportunities for Commerce and Key Economic Developments Act of 2025.
  • S.3219 – Albuquerque Indian School Act of 2026.

Senator Murkowski then spoke on the Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act.

3:24 p.m. Senator Scott (FL) spoke on socialism.

3:14 p.m. Senator Grassley spoke on the Working Families Tax Cuts Act and cancer screening.

3:04 p.m. Senator Hawley achieved unanimous consent to pass the following bills en bloc:

  • H.R.1945, America’s National Churchill Museum National Historic Landmark Act.
  • H.R.1550, Strengthening America’s Turning Point Act.

Senator Hawley then spoke about the Winston Churchill Memorial, located at Westminster College in Fulton, Missouri.

3:03 p.m. By a vote of 48-51, the Senate did not agree to the motion to proceed to S.J.Res.197 (Baldwin Obamacare Exchange Standards CRA).

  • Republican Senator Collins voted in favor.
  • Senator Sullivan didn’t vote.

2:21 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on the motion to proceed to S.J.Res.197, Baldwin Obamacare Exchange Standards CRA.

2:15 p.m. Senator Baldwin spoke on the Affordable Care Act.

2:15 p.m. The Senate returned from recess. There will be up to 10 minutes of debate on a motion to proceed to S. J. Res. 197, Baldwin Obamacare Exchange Standards CRA.

12:30 p.m. The Senate is now in recess.

12:21 p.m. Senator Welch spoke on tariffs.

12:06 p.m. Senator Crapo achieved unanimous consent for the Senate to have 10 minutes of debate before the scheduled vote at 2:15 p.m. today.

11:34 a.m. Senator Banks spoke on Dystonia, a muscle movement disorder. He then received unanimous consent for the Senate to adopt S.Res.917 to designate the month of September as Dystonia Awareness Month.

11:32 a.m. Senator Kim spoke on AI competition with China and safety regulations.

11:30 a.m. Senator Schatz spoke on safety and guidelines for AI.

11:21 a.m. Senator Warner spoke on the concerns of AI chatbots. He then asked unanimous consent to pass the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act at the Secretary’s desk; Senator Cruz reserved the right to object. Senator Cruz objected. Senator Warner spoke more on a potential AI safety board.

11:17 a.m. Senator Kim spoke on AI and national security.

11:10 a.m. Senator Schatz spoke on AI regulations.

11:03 a.m. Senator Warner spoke on artificial intelligence regulations and progress.

10:50 a.m. Leader Schumer spoke on the need for guardrails on artificial intelligence.

10:40 a.m. Senator Barasso spoke on lowering costs for Americans.

10:25 a.m. Leader Thune called up and spoke in favor of H.R. 9340, A bill to amend the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to establish a federal standard relating to the recovery of the full, incremental costs of upgrades that serve large-load customers, and for other purposes.

The Senate will convene at 10:00 a.m. and be in a period of morning business.

The Senate will recess from 12:30 — 2:15 p.m. to accommodate the weekly conference meetings.

At 2:15 p.m., we expect the Senate will vote on the motion to proceed to S.J.Res.197, Baldwin Obamacare Exchange Standards CRA.

Further votes are expected.

Cloture was filed on the following items in the following order on Monday evening:

1.     Motion to proceed to H.R.7008, Stop Insider Trading Act.

2.     Motion to proceed to H.R.9340, Ratepayer Protection Act.

3.     The nomination of Keith Sonderling to be Secretary of Labor.

10:57 p.m. The Senate stands adjourned under the provisions of S.Res.913, as a further mark of respect to the former Senator Nancy Kassebaum. The Senate will convene on Tuesday, September 29th at 10:00 a.m. Following Leader remarks, the Senate will be in a period of Morning Business with Senators permitted to speak therein for up to 10 minutes each.

The Senate will recess from 12:30 p.m. to 2:15 p.m. to allow for weekly caucus meetings.

At 2:15 p.m. the Senate is expected to proceed to a roll call vote on the motion to proceed to S.J.Res.197, Baldwin Obamacare Exchange Standards CRA.

Further roll call votes are expected during Tuesday’s session.

Wrap-up:

  • H.R.10167- Common Cents Act; passed by unanimous consent.
  • S.2339 – EARLY Act Reauthorization, as amended; passed by unanimous consent.
  • H.R.8205 – Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act; passed by voice vote.
  • S.4009 – Falun Gong and Victims of Forced Organ Harvesting Protection Act, as amended; passed by unanimous consent.
  • S.4974 – Making America’s Food Safer Act, as amended; passed by unanimous consent.
  • S.4395 – Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Reauthorization Act; passed by unanimous consent.
  • H.R.997 – National Taxpayer Advocate Enhancement Act; passed by unanimous consent.
  • H.R. 7730 – Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act; passed by unanimous consent.
  • S.Res. 913 – Former Senator Kassebaum; adopted by unanimous consent.
  • Agreed to the following by unanimous consent en bloc:
    • S.Res.914 – National Cholesterol Education Month
    • S.Res.915 – Prison Fellowship 50th Anniversary
    • S.Res.916 – Farm Safety Week

******

10:26 p.m. Senator Merkley spoke on President Trump’s arch project and asked unanimous consent for the Senate to pass the bill at the desk related to President Trump’s arch project. Senator Lee objected. Senator Merkley then spoke on the Kennedy Center and asked unanimous consent for the Senate to pass the bill that is at the desk related to the demolition of memorials. Senator Lee objected.

10:22 p.m. Majority Leader Thune filed cloture on the following:

  • Motion to proceed to H.R.7008, Stop Insider Trading Act.
  • Motion to proceed to H.R.9340, Ratepayer Protection Act.
  • Nomination of Keith Sonderling to be Secretary of Labor.

10:21 p.m. The Senate adopted S.Res.913, relating to the death of the Honorable Nancy Kassebaum, former United States Senator from the State of Kansas, by unanimous consent.

10:16 p.m. Senator Moran spoke on the Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

10:14 p.m. Senator Coons spoke on the Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

10:02 p.m. Senator Cantwell spoke on the Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

10:02 p.m. Senator Cantwell clarified the anti-trust exemption regarding the Protect College Sports Act of 2026. Senator Coons verified the intent of the legislation.

10:01 p.m. By a vote of 77-22, the Senate passed S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026, as amended.

  • Senators voting No: Alsobrooks, Blumenthal, Blunt Rochester, Booker, Duckworth, Gillibrand, Kaine, Kelly, Kim, Markey, Merkley, Murphy, Paul (R), Reed, Sanders, Schiff, Schumer, Scott – FL (R), Van Hollen, Warnock, Warren, and Whitehouse.
  • Senator Sullivan did not vote.

9:41 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on passage of S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026, as amended.

9:41 p.m. Senator Booker spoke against the Protect College Sports Act.

9:41 p.m. Senator Cantwell spoke in support of the Protect College Sports Act.

9:40 p.m. Senator Cruz spoke in support of the Protect College Sports Act.

9:40 p.m. By a vote of 47-52, the Senate did not agree to the Booker amendment #6835 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

  • Republican Senator Britt voted in favor.
  • Senator Sullivan did not vote.

9:21 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on adoption of Booker amendment #6835 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

9:18 p.m. By a vote of 49-50, the #Senate did not agree to Booker amendment #6805 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

Republican senators voting in favor: Collins and Hawley.

Senator not voting: Sullivan.

8:41 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on Booker amendment #6805 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

8:40 p.m. Senator Cantwell spoke in favor of Booker amendment #6805.

8:39 p.m. Senator Cruz spoke against Booker amendment #6805.

8:36 p.m. Senator Booker called up his amendment #6805 and spoke on it.

8:36 p.m. The Senate adopted Moody/Blumenthal amendment #6831 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026 by voice vote.

8:35 p.m. Senator Blumenthal spoke in support of amendment #6831.

8:33 p.m. Senator Moody called up her amendment #6831 and spoke on it.

8:33 p.m. By a vote of 42-54, the Senate did not agree to the Kennedy amendment #6760 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026. (60-vote affirmative threshold).

  • Republican senators voting in favor: Banks, Cramer, Graham, Hawley, Husted, Hyde-Smith, Kennedy, Murkowski, and Wicker.
  • Democrat senators voting No: Booker, Cantwell, Durbin, Fetterman, Hickenlooper, Kaine, Kim, Klobuchar, Ossoff, Rosen, Schatz, Warner, and Whitehouse.
  • Senators not voting: Lee, Sullivan, Tillis, and Tuberville.

8:08 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on the Kennedy amendment #6760 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026. (60-vote affirmative threshold)

8:04 p.m. Senator Kennedy spoke supporting his amendment #6760 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (60-vote affirmative threshold).

8:04 p.m. By a vote of 1-94, the Senate did not agree to the Paul amendment #6758 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

  • Senator Paul voted yes.
  • Not voting: Senators Cornyn, Lee, Sullivan, Tillis and Warner.

7:38 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on Paul amendment #6758 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

7:37 p.m. Senator Cantwell spoke against the Paul amendment.

7:36 p.m. Senator Paul called up his amendment #6758.

7:34 p.m. Senator Scott (SC) called up his amendment #6830 and the Senate adopted it by voice vote.

7:34 p.m. By a vote of 96-1, the Senate adopted Baldwin amendment #6828 to Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

  • Senator Tuberville voted No.
  • Senators not voting: Banks, Cornyn, and Sullivan.

6:41 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on the Baldwin amendment #6828.

6:40 p.m. Senator Baldwin spoke supporting her amendment.

6:38 p.m. Senator Cruz got unanimous consent for the following:

Up to 8 roll call votes on the following in relation to Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026:

  1. Baldwin amendment #6828
  2. Scott (SC) amendment #6830
  3. Paul amendment #6758
  4. Kennedy amendment #6760 (60-vote affirmative threshold)
  5. Moody-Blumenthal amendment #6831
  6. Booker amendment #6805
  7. Booker amendment #6835
  8. Passage of Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026, as amended.

5:45 p.m. Senator Cantwell spoke on the Protect College Sports Act.

5:38 p.m. Senator Cruz spoke on the Protect College Sports Act.

5:03 p.m. Senator Booker spoke on the Protect College Sports Act.

4:46 p.m. Senator Schmitt spoke on the Protect College Sports Act.

4:36 p.m. Senator Coons spoke on the Protect College Sports Act.

4:16 p.m. Senator Kennedy spoke on the Protect College Sports Act. He then spoke on the cost of heavy machinery and ships.

4:03 p.m. Senator Murphy spoke against the Protect College Sports Act.

3:42 p.m. Senator Durbin spoke on President Truman, Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding, Iran, President Trump’s rescission requests and projects, and elections.

3:35 p.m. Minority Leader Schumer spoke on President Trump’s TV ads and building projects. He also spoke on Iran.

3:13 p.m. Majority Leader Thune spoke on small businesses and the Working Families Tax Cuts bill.

3:00 p.m. The Senate convened.

******

The Senate will convene at 3:00 p.m. and resume consideration of S.4668, the college sports bill post-cloture.

At 5:30 p.m., the Senate will vote on passage of S.4668.

content.rendered:
4:05 p.m. The Senate adjourned and will reconvene at 3:00 p.m. on Monday, September 28. They will resume consideration of S. 4668, the Protect College Sports Act and vote on passage of the bill at 5:30 p.m.

During wrap-up:

H.R. 9340- Ratepayer Protection Act. Second reading and placed on the calendar.

Passed by unanimous consent:

  • S. 3257-John A. Hauser Mental Health in Aviation Act with a Hoeven substitute amendment
  • S. 3258-Aviation Medication Transparency Act of 2026
  • Motion to Concur in the House amendment to S.283 – Illegal Red Snapper and Tuna Enforcement Act
  • H.R.2388 – Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe Project Lands Restoration Act
  • Motion to Concur in the House amendment to S.240 – Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025

The following resolutions were agreed to en bloc:

  • S.Res.902 – Telehealth Awareness Week
  • S.Res.903 – Nuclear Weapons Workers Day of Remembrance
  • S.Res.904 – Gold Star Families Week
  • S.Res.905 – Lobster Day

3:35 p.m. Senators Warner, Schatz and Kim spoke about AI.

3:15 p.m. Senator Warnock paid tribute to his departing Chief of Staff.

2:53 p.m. Senator Duckworth paid tribute to to her departing staffer, Kalina Thompson.

2:40 p.m. Senator Fischer spoke about the Farm Bill.

2:39 p.m. By a vote of 49-50, the Senate did not adopt H.Con.Res.89 – War Powers Resolution (Iran).

  • GOP Senators in favor: Collins, Murkowski, Paul, and Tillis
  • Senator Fetterman (D) voted no.
  • Senators not voting: Alsobrooks .

1:45 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on the adoption of H.Con.Res.89 – War Powers Resolution (Iran).

1:41 p.m. Senator Kaine spoke on the war with Iran.

1:32 p.m. Senator Baldwin spoke on diesel.

1:20 p.m. Senators Klobuchar and Murphy spoke about the Iran war powers resolution.

1:10 p.m. Senator Merkley spoke about Chinese authoritarianism and the freedom of speech. He asked for unanimous consent to proceed to and pass S. 226. Senator Paul objected.

12:57 p.m. Senators Slotkin and Moreno spoke about Chinese cars.

12:43 p.m. Senators Kim and Schiff spoke about the Iran war powers resolution.

12:40 p.m. By a vote of 74-25 the motion to invoke cloture on S. 4658 (Protect College Sports Act) was agreed to. Voting no: Alsobrooks, Blumenthal, Blunt Rochester, Booker, Duckworth, Gillibrand, Hirono, Kaine, Kelly, Kim, Markey, Merkley, Moody-R, Murphy, Paul-R, Reed, Sanders, Schiff, Schumer, Scott-FL-R, Van Hollen, Warnock, Warren, Whitehouse, and Wyden. Senator Tillis did not vote.

11:46 a.m. The Senate began voting on the motion to invoke cloture on S.4658, the Protect College Sports Act.

11:45 a.m. By a vote of 77-23, the Senate adopted the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668 (Protect College Sports Act). Senators voting no: Alsobrooks, Blumenthal, Blunt Rochester, Booker, Duckworth, Gillibrand, Hirono, Kaine, Kelly, Kim, Markey, Merkley, Moody-R, Murphy, Paul-R, Reed, Sanders, Schiff, Schumer, Scott-FL-R, Van Hollen, Warnock, and Warren.

10:47 a.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on adoption of the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668 (Protect College Sports Act).

10:46 a.m. Senator Barrasso made a motion to table amendment #6779 to S.4668 (Protect College Sports Act) and it was agreed to by voice vote. Senator Barrasso then made a motion to table amendment #6777 to S.4668 and it was agreed to by voice vote. Senator Barrasso received unanimous consent for the Senate to vote on adoption of H.Con.Res.89, War Powers Resolution (Iran), at 1:45 p.m. today.

10:30 a.m. Minority Leader Schumer spoke on the White House press ban.

10:15 a.m. Majority Leader Thune spoke on the economy and cost of living.

10:03 a.m. Senator Grassley spoke on fraud prevention.

10:00 a.m. The Senate has convened. Leadership time is reserved and the Senate has resumed consideration of the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, the college sports bill, post-cloture.

The Senate will convene at 10:00 a.m. and resume consideration of the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to S.4668, the college sports bill, post-cloture.

At 10:45 a.m., the Senate will proceed to two votes:

  1. Adoption of the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment.
  2. Cloture on S.4668, the college sports bill, as amended, if amended.

Further votes are expected.

7:28 p.m. The Senate stands adjourned until 10:00 a.m. tomorrow and in honor of the late Senator Jon Kyl. With Leader Remarks reserved, the Senate will immediately resume consideration of the Cruz-Cantwell amendment #6776 to S.4668.

Votes scheduled: At 10:45am, on Thursday, September 24th, the Senate will proceed to two roll call votes on the following:
1. Motion to invoke cloture on Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026, as amended, if amended.
2. Adoption of Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026.
Additional votes are possible.

  • Confirmed by unanimous consent: Cal #918, #119, and PN769-2 Wade E. Arnold on the Secretary’s Desk in the Coast Guard.
  • Received its first reading: H.R. 9430 – American Drone Manufacturing Dominance Act of 2026
  • Passed by UC: S. 1962 -Secure Space Act of 2026. as amended.
  • Passed by UC: S. 3404, – Satellite Cybersecurity Act of 2025, as amended.
  • Agreed to by S. Res. 863 – A resolution expressing support for designation of the week of September 13 through 19, 2026, as “National Adult Education and Family Literacy Week”
  • Agreed to by UC en bloc: S. Res. 888, S. Res. 892, S. Res. 893, S. Res. 894, S. Res. 895, S. Res. 896
  • Agreed to by UC: S. Res. 897 – Honoring the life and legacy of former Senator Jon Kyl of Arizona

7:21 p.m. Senator Lummis wrapped up.

6:40 p.m. Senator Bennet spoke on vaccine schedules for children.

6:09 p.m. Senator Sullivan spoke on his bill related to fishing and bycatch reduction. He then asked unanimous consent to pass S.4938, as amended by the Sullivan amendment at the desk; Senator Markey reserved the right to object and spoke on fisheries. Senator Markey then objected.

5:51 p.m. Senator Whitehouse spoke on climate change and wildfires and asked unanimous consent to take up and pass S. Res. 559; Senator Scott of Florida objected.

5:40 p.m. Senator Blumenthal asked unanimous consent to pass H.R.2550; Senator Scott-Fl objected.

5:37 p.m. Senator Kaine spoke on federal workers.

5:35 p.m. Senator Alsobrooks spoke on federal workers.

5:34 p.m. Senator Blumenthal spoke on federal workers.

5:05 p.m. Senator Hickenlooper spoke on the war with Iran.

4:11 p.m. Senator Schatz spoke on AI.

4:02 p.m. Senator McCormick spoke on the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia and AI.

3:42 p.m. Senator Blackburn spoke on dating site scams and achieved unanimous consent for passage H.R. 2481, Romance Scam Prevention Act.

3:32 p.m. Senator Justice spoke on childhood cancer and achieved unanimous consent for passage of S.2933, a bill to redesignate a playground in the New River Gorge National Park and Preserve in the State of West Virginia as the “Hearts of Gold Playground: In Honor of West Virginia Children and Families Impacted by Childhood Cancer”.

3:23 p.m. Senator Lujan spoke about the New Mexico Land Grant and Cooperation Act and achieved unanimous consent for passage of S.1363, New Mexico Land Grant-Mercedes Historical or Traditional Use Cooperation and Coordination Act, as amended.

3:17 p.m. Senator Shaheen spoke on China’s support of Iran.

3:16 p.m. By a party-line vote of 50-47, the Senate confirmed Angela Veronica Colmenero to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

  • Not voting: Senators Daines, Ernst and Tillis.

2:16 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on confirmation of Executive Calendar #828, Angela Veronica Colmenero to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

2:15 p.m. The Senate returned from recess.

12:43 p.m. The Senate recessed until 2:15 p.m.

12:26 p.m. Senators Marshall and Cassidy spoke on the cost of health care and asked unanimous consent to take up and pass S. 2355, on that topic. Senator Paul objected.

11:54 a.m. Senator Lee spoke on election security and asked unanimous consent to take up and pass S. 5271, on this topic. Senator Padilla asked UC to modify the request to take up and pass S. 5390. Senator Lee objected to the modification, and Senator Padilla objected to the initial request.

11:46 a.m. Senator Ernst spoke on college sports. She then spoke on critical minerals and military supply chains. Senator Ernst then received unanimous consent to pass H.R.1721 – Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act.

11:35 a.m. Senator Coons spoke on college sports.

11:19 a.m. Senator Durbin spoke on DACA students.

11:00 a.m. Senator Paul spoke about college sports. He then made an unanimous consent request to call up his amendment #6758 to S. 4668; Senator Barrasso objected.

10:49 a.m. Senator Barrasso spoke about China.

10:41 a.m. Senator Schumer spoke about the retirement AFSCME president Lee Saunders. He also spoke about China and AI and also tariffs and farmers.

10:22 a.m. Senator Thune spoke about socialism.

10:05 a.m. Senator Grassley spoke about the Working Families Tax Cut.

10:00 a.m. The Senate convened.

The Senate will convene at 10:00 a.m. and resume consideration of Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026, post-cloture.

The Senate will recess from 12:30 p.m. until 2:15 p.m. for the weekly conference meetings.

At 2:15 p.m., the Senate will proceed to a roll call vote on confirmation of Executive Calendar #828, Angela Veronica Colmenero, of Texas, to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas. Please note, further roll call votes are possible during Wednesday’s session of the Senate.

8:00 p.m. The Senate stands adjourned and will convene at 10:00am on Wednesday to resume consideration of Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026, post-cloture. The Senate will recess from 12:30pm until 2:15pm for the weekly conference meetings. At 2:15pm, the Senate will proceed to a roll call vote on confirmation of Executive Calendar #828, Angela Veronica Colmenero, of Texas, to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

Please note, further roll call votes are possible during Wednesday’s session of the Senate. 

In today’s session of the Senate:

Roll Call Votes

Motion to invoke cloture on Executive Calendar #828, Angela Veronica Colmenero, of Texas, to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas. Invoked (52-43)

Motion to invoke cloture on Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776 to Cal. #449, S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026. Invoked (70-21)

Wrap Up

S.Res.870- Hispanic Heritage Month

S.Res.871- National Purple Heart Recognition Day H.R.4467 – Vicksburg National Military Park Boundary

7:33 p.m. Senator Scott-Fl spoke on immigration.

7:32 p.m. By a vote of 70-21, the Senate invoked cloture on the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776, to S. 4668. Senators not voting: Cassidy, Coons, Gallego, Kim, Murphy, Schatz, Tillis, Tuberville, and Whitehouse. Senators voting no: Alsobrooks, Blumenthal, Blunt Rochester, Booker, Duckworth, Durbin, Gillibrand, Kaine, Kelly, Markey, Merkley, Moody (R), Paul (R), Reed, Sanders, Schiff, Schumer, Scott-FL (R), Van Hollen, Warnock, and Warren.

6:38 p.m. The Senate began voting on cloture on the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment #6776, to S. 4668, the Protect College Sports Act.

6:36 p.m. By a party-line vote of 52-43, the Senate invoked cloture on the Colmenero nomination. Senators not voting: Cassidy, Coons, Gallego, Murphy and Whitehouse.

5:41 p.m. The Senate began voting on cloture on the nomination of Angela Colmenero to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

5:29 p.m. Senator Cruz spoke o the sports bill.

5:20 p.m. Senator Cantwell spoke on the Save our Sports Act.

5:02 Senator Kelly spoke on AI.

4:43 p.m. Senator Tuberville spoke on gender identity.

4:42 p.m. Senator Barrasso received unanimous consent for the following time agreements:

  1. If cloture is invoked on the Colmenero nomination that all post-cloture time be expired and, that the Senate vote on confirmation at a time to be determined by the Majority Leader no later than Friday, September 25.
  2. If cloture is invoked on the Cruz-Cantwell Substitute Amendment #6776 to S. 4668, that all time during adjournment, recess, morning business, and leader remarks count towards post-cloture.

4:25 p.m. Senator Murray spoke on the economy.

4:18 p.m. Senator Wicker spoke on the impending visit of Chinese President Xi. He then spoke on human rights in China.

3:57 p.m. Senator Budd paid tribute to the departing Director of the Marine Corps Senate Liaison Office, Colonel Robert Sucher. He then spoke on the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping.

3:39 p.m. Senator Durbin spoke on free press in America and Pastor Ezra Jin.

3:24 p.m. Minority Leader Schumer spoke on AI and Iran.

3:09 p.m. Majority Leader Thune spoke on Democrat policies in California.

3:04 p.m. Senator Grassley spoke on ethanol.

3:00 p.m. The Senate convened.

******

The Senate will convene at 3:00 p.m. and following any Leader remarks will resume consideration of the nomination of Angela Veronica Colmenero to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

At 5:30 p.m. the Senate will vote on the motion to invoke cloture on the Colmenero nomination.

Further votes are possible during today’s session.

*****

Sports bill: S.4668: Cloture has been filed on S.4668, the sports bill and the Cruz-Cantwell substitute amendment (6776) to S.4668.

The Senate began the Rule 14 process of placing the following bill directly on the Calendar:

  • A bill to ratify and approve all authorizations, permits, verifications, extensions, biological opinions, incidental take statements, and any other approvals or orders issued pursuant to Federal law necessary for the establishment and administration of the Coastal Plain oil and gas leasing program, and for other purposes. (S.5438)
  • A bill to establish the National Fraud Enforcement Division of the Department of Justice. (H.R.9576)

content.rendered:
3:45 p.m. The Senate adjourned and will convene for a pro forma session only at 9:00 a.m. on Friday, September 18 with no business to be conducted.

When the Senate adjourns following the pro forma, it will next convene for business at 3:00 p.m. on Tuesday, September 22nd. Following Leader remarks, the Senate will resume consideration of the nomination of Angela Veronica Colmenero to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.

At 5:30 p.m., the Senate will proceed to a roll call vote on the motion to invoke cloture on the Colmenero nomination.

Further roll call votes are possible during Tuesday’s session.

******

3:37 p.m. Senator Lummis wrapped up.

The following bills received their first reading en bloc:

  1. S.5348 – Alaska Right to Produce Act
  2. H.R. 9576 – National Fraud Enforcement Division Act of 2026
  • Passed by unanimous consent: H.R. 5345 – Improving Social Security’s Service to Victims of Identity Theft Act
  • Agreed to by unanimous consent: S.Res.862 – A resolution honoring the life of Dolly Parton.
  • Agreed to by UC: S.Res.816 – Honoring the independence of countries in Central Asia.

3:15 p.m. Majority Leader Thune filed cloture on the following:

  1. Nomination of Angela Veronica Colmenero to be United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas.
  2. Cruz-Cantwell Substitute Amendment #6776 to S. 4668
  3. S. 4668 – Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

Majority Leader Thune also filled the amendment tree for S. 4668.

3:13 p.m. By a vote of 49-45, the Senate confirmed Kasdin Miller Mitchell to be United States District Judge for the Northern District of Texas.

  • Party-line vote with Senators Marshall, McConnell, Moran, Shaheen, Tuberville and Van Hollen not voting.

1:57 p.m. The Senate began a roll call vote on the confirmation of Kasdin Miller Mitchell to be United States District Judge for the Northern District of Texas.

1:44 p.m. Senator Heinrich spoke on AI. Senator Husted also spoke on AI and then asked unanimous consent that the Senate pass H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act. Senator Heinrich asked unanimous consent for a modification. Senator Husted objected to the modification; Senator Heinrich then objected to the original request.

1:38 p.m. Senator Moody spoke on constitutional rights.

1:37 p.m. By a vote of 49-47, the Senate invoked cloture on the nomination of Kasdin Miller Mitchell to be United States District Judge for the Northern District of Texas.

  • The vote was party-line vote with Senators Hagerty, McConnell, Moran, and Tuberville not voting.

12:53 p.m. The Senate is now voting on the motion to invoke cloture on the nomination of Kasdin Miller Mitchell to be United States District Judge for the Northern District of Texas.

12:52 p.m. By a vote of 77-22, the Senate agreed to the motion to proceed to S.4668, Protect College Sports Act of 2026.

5:58 p.m. The Senate stands adjourned until 10:00 a.m. on Thursday.

5:54 p.m. Senator Moreno achieved the following during wrap up:

  • Adopted by unanimous consent: S.Res.847 – Pennsylvania State University Men’s Wrestling.
  • Adopted by unanimous consent en bloc: S.Res.859 – 9/11 25th Anniversary, S.Res.860 – National Voter Registration Day, and S.Res.861 – Oklahoma University Baseball Championship.

5:15 p.m. Senator Kennedy spoke on artificial intelligence development. He then asked unanimous consent to pass S.5417; Senator Paul reserved the right to object. Senator Paul asked unanimous consent to modify Senator Kennedy’s request; Senator Kennedy reserved the right to object. Senator Kennedy then objected to Senator Paul’s request; Senator Paul then objected to Senator Kennedy’s original request.

3:25 p.m. Senator Blackburn spoke on the Memphis Crime Taskforce.

2:13 p.m. Minority Leader Schumer spoke on tariffs.

1:51 p.m. Senator Murray spoke about tariffs.

1:38 p.m. Senator Grassley spoke about University of Northern Iowa

1:26 p.m. Senator Hickenlooper spoke about housing costs.

12:19 p.m. Senator Peters spoke on the 988 suicide and crisis lifeline.

11:08 a.m. By voice vote, the Senate passed H.R.7250 – To reauthorize the Fort Peck Reservation Rural Water System Act of 2000 (Daines). By unanimous consent, the Senate passed. H.R.3657 – Hydropower Licensing Transparency Act (Cortez Masto).

11:05 a.m. Senator Cortez Masto spoke on hydropower and commerce.

11:03 a.m. Senator Daines spoke on two bills with Senator Cortez Masto on hydropower energy and commerce.

10:51 a.m. Senator Barrasso spoke on energy.

10:44 a.m. Minority Leader Schumer spoke on tariffs, Iran, and interest rates.

10:19 a.m. Majority Leader Thune spoke on the Protect College Sports Act.

10:02 a.m. Senator Grassley spoke on his 99 county meetings.

The Senate will convene at 10:00 a.m. and resume consideration of the motion to proceed to S.4668, the Protect College Sports Act, post-cloture.

All time during recess, adjournment, Leader remarks and morning business count post-cloture on the motion to proceed.

Votes are possible.

*****

Cloture will ripen on Wednesday on the nomination of Kasdin Mitchell to be a US District Judge for the Northern District of Texas.    

UC agreement: No later than Friday, October 2nd, H.Con.Res.89 (war powers regarding Iran) will be discharged from the Committee on Foreign Relations and the Senate will proceed to its consideration; with up to 6 hours for debate only, and following the use or yielding back of that time, the Senate vote on adoption of the concurrent resolution.
